around Korea with his family. This is his food diary.
July 25
We went to Damyang and visited Jungnogwon, a
famous bamboo garden. We enjoyed walking in the
garden. After we looked around, we ate two local
dishes, daetongbap and tteokgalbi. Daetongbap is
rice in a bamboo bowl. I loved its unique bamboo
smell. Tteokgalbi, a Korean beef dish, was soft and
sweet. The dishes really went well together.
July 30
We visited Tongyeong and went up the mountain
by cable car. Seeing the blue ocean and the green
islands was fantastic! Near the sea, we found a local
restaurant and ate chungmugimbap. It wasn’t like
other types of gimbap. There was only rice inside
the seaweed. Kimchi and spicy squid were on the
side. It was spicy but really delicious. I heard about
the history of this food. Tongyeong is an old name
for Chungmu. Long ago, fishermen in this town
started to eat chungmugimbap because it did not
go bad quickly.

board in Jeju’s language.

be at my grandma’s all summer.”
“I’ll plant my aster and your zinnia side by side,”
El said.

smiled.

growing season. All summer long, she cared for
them.
On the last day of summer, Jo came to El’s house.
El and Jo ran to the garden and suddenly stopped.
Something was DIFFERENT! (A)과꽃에 꽃들이 있었다

El and Jo were the (A)[tallest / smallest] students
in the class. They were always together. They even
watered the plants together in the class because
they could not reach the pots alone.
However, in the spring, something was DIFFERENT.
Jo grew TALLER! Jo was taller than El, so Jo could
water the plants alone. El felt (B)[more confident /
smaller] every day.
On the last day of school, Mr. Diaz said, “Class,
you can take a flower home and care for it over
the summer.” All the students ran to the window.
El’s classmates reached for the pots over tiny El.
They took all the pots with colorful flowers.
El took the last pot. It had the smallest plant with
no flowers. “I feel just like you, (C)[giant / little]
plant,” said El. Mr. Diaz looked at El and said,
“That’s an aster plant. In time, it’ll grow and have
beautiful flowers.”
(A)
(B)
(C)

When Matisse became an old man, he fell ill. He
could only lie in bed and sleep. He couldn’t paint
at all. He could only paint in his dreams. When
Matisse opened his eyes, they were full of sadness.
Luckily, before long, he could sit. A little later, he
started to paint again. (A)___________, he realized
that he couldn’t paint well anymore.
